intro: Here, in Sinop province, lies Sinope, an ancient city whose story runs from the 7th century BC to today. It was the oldest Greek colony on the Black Sea, the birthplace of Diogenes, and the city that lent its name to the pigment sinopia.
history: Sinope was founded by Milesian settlers in the 7th century BC, and it soon became a key port of Black Sea trade. Xenophon mentions it in his Anabasis. From Roman to Seljuk times the city never lost its calling: it remained, through every change of rule, a maritime centre.
structure-1: You are now before Sinop Castle. These Byzantine and Seljuk walls stand guard over the northern coast of the Sinop peninsula, as they have for centuries.
structure-2: Here are the remains of the ancient theatre, set into the hillside. Pause for a moment and imagine the audience gathering on its slope.
structure-3: This is Balatlar Church, a Byzantine church in Sinop. Look closely: it was built over the remains of a Roman building, one age laid directly upon another.
structure-4: Now to the Serapeum, a sanctuary and temple complex dedicated to the Egyptian god Serapis — a reminder of how far the ties of this port city reached.
structure-5: And finally, Sinop Museum, where the archaeological finds from Sinop and its surroundings are displayed. Here the story you have walked through comes together in objects.
facts: Did you know? The Cynic philosopher Diogenes was born here, and the city lent its name to the reddish pigment sinopia. Diogenes lived in a jar, and when Alexander asked him what he wanted, he simply replied, 'stand out of my light'. Sinope also has the only naturally sheltered harbour on the Black Sea, which made it first a Milesian colony and later the Pontic naval base. And Mithridates VI, the king who held out longest against Rome, was born here too.
outro: This brings our journey through Sinope to an end. Please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. May the sea wind that has blown here since the first settlers arrived go with you. Enjoy your visit.
